texts.label: text
texts.orig: How to Report Incidents and Actively Exploited Vulnerabilities via the Single Reporting Platform (SRP)
texts.text: How to Report Incidents and Actively Exploited Vulnerabilities via the Single Reporting Platform (SRP)

texts.label: text
texts.orig: As of 11 September 2026, the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) requires manufacturers to report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents having an impact on the security of products with digital elements sold in the EU market.
texts.text: As of 11 September 2026, the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) requires manufacturers to report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents having an impact on the security of products with digital elements sold in the EU market.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The CRA also requires open-source software stewards to report those events to the extent that they are involved in the development of products with digital elements.
texts.text: The CRA also requires open-source software stewards to report those events to the extent that they are involved in the development of products with digital elements.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: What are your new reporting obligations?
texts.text: What are your new reporting obligations?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The CRA Single Reporting Platform (SRP) is an online tool for manufacturers and open-source software stewards to meet the obligation to report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents. Designed to simplify EU reporting obligations, the CRA SRP is an electronic system to report only once to communicate to all relevant authorities. The platform incorporates security measures to protect confidentiality.
texts.text: The CRA Single Reporting Platform (SRP) is an online tool for manufacturers and open-source software stewards to meet the obligation to report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents. Designed to simplify EU reporting obligations, the CRA SRP is an electronic system to report only once to communicate to all relevant authorities. The platform incorporates security measures to protect confidentiality.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Which national CSIRT should you report to?
texts.text: Which national CSIRT should you report to?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: In general, the national CSIRT to which you should report through the SRP is primarily determined by your main location of establishment. Article 14(7) of the CRA provides detailed information allowing you to identify the national CSIRT to report to.
texts.text: In general, the national CSIRT to which you should report through the SRP is primarily determined by your main location of establishment. Article 14(7) of the CRA provides detailed information allowing you to identify the national CSIRT to report to.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: When do you need to report such events?
texts.text: When do you need to report such events?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The reporting process starts the moment you, as a manufacturer or OSS steward, become aware of an active exploitation of a vulnerability or severe incident. Adhering to the following timelines:
texts.text: The reporting process starts the moment you, as a manufacturer or OSS steward, become aware of an active exploitation of a vulnerability or severe incident. Adhering to the following timelines:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Within 24 hours of becoming aware of the vulnerability or incident.
texts.text: Within 24 hours of becoming aware of the vulnerability or incident.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Actively Exploited Vulnerability / Severe Incident Notification
texts.text: Actively Exploited Vulnerability / Severe Incident Notification

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Within 72 hours of becoming aware, providing general information and an initial assessment.
texts.text: Within 72 hours of becoming aware, providing general information and an initial assessment.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: For vulnerabilities : No later than 14 days after a corrective measure (e.g. patch) is available.
texts.text: For vulnerabilities : No later than 14 days after a corrective measure (e.g. patch) is available.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: For severe incidents : Within 1 month after the submission of the 72-hour Actively Exploited Vulnerability / Severe Incident Notification
texts.text: For severe incidents : Within 1 month after the submission of the 72-hour Actively Exploited Vulnerability / Severe Incident Notification

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Each notification allows sending information automatically to your national CSIRT that initially receives the notification, the other national CSIRTs where the Product with digital elements is available, and to the EU Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA).
texts.text: Each notification allows sending information automatically to your national CSIRT that initially receives the notification, the other national CSIRTs where the Product with digital elements is available, and to the EU Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA).

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: What events are you obliged to report?
texts.text: What events are you obliged to report?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Actively Exploited Vulnerabilities: Vulnerabilities in products with digital elements that are known to be currently exploited by a malicious actor, in accordance with Article 3(42) of the CRA.
texts.text: Actively Exploited Vulnerabilities: Vulnerabilities in products with digital elements that are known to be currently exploited by a malicious actor, in accordance with Article 3(42) of the CRA.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Severe Incidents: Incidents that have a severe impact on the security of the product with digital elements (e.g., compromising availability, authenticity, integrity, or confidentiality) in accordance with Article 3(44); the criteria for severity are defined in Article 14(5).
texts.text: Severe Incidents: Incidents that have a severe impact on the security of the product with digital elements (e.g., compromising availability, authenticity, integrity, or confidentiality) in accordance with Article 3(44); the criteria for severity are defined in Article 14(5).

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: What happens once notifications are submitted?
texts.text: What happens once notifications are submitted?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Once notifications are submitted, the CSIRT initially receiving the notification will then disseminate the information without delay to other relevant CSIRTs in EU Member States where the product is also available. The notification is simultaneously made available to ENISA.
texts.text: Once notifications are submitted, the CSIRT initially receiving the notification will then disseminate the information without delay to other relevant CSIRTs in EU Member States where the product is also available. The notification is simultaneously made available to ENISA.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: National CSIRTs will also share some information with their respective market surveillance authorities to enable them to fulfil their enforcement obligations.
texts.text: National CSIRTs will also share some information with their respective market surveillance authorities to enable them to fulfil their enforcement obligations.

texts.orig: How would you use the platform?
texts.text: How would you use the platform?

texts.orig: For further information consult the ENISA SRP FAQ page https://www.enisa.europa.eu/cra-srp , which also includes references to the 'European Commission's guidance on the CRA', which in section 9.1 includes further clarifications on reporting obligations.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Can dissemination of information be delayed?
texts.text: Can dissemination of information be delayed?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Yes, under exceptional circumstances the dissemination of information may be delayed, pursuant to Article 16(2) of the CRA. Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/881 further specifies the conditions under which the dissemination of notifications may be delayed.
texts.text: Yes, under exceptional circumstances the dissemination of information may be delayed, pursuant to Article 16(2) of the CRA. Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/881 further specifies the conditions under which the dissemination of notifications may be delayed.
